facts.text: Riverbank began as a ferry crossing and grew into a town when the San Francisco and San Joaquin Valley Railroad arrived, later taken over by Santa Fe.
The city’s name comes from its position on the Stanislaus River, a fact that still echoes in its riverfront parks.
The Riverbank Historical Society, founded in 1992, preserves local history in the 1916 Riverbank Bank building, now a museum and archive.
Riverbank’s Branch Library earned a spot on the National Register of Historic Places, highlighting its architectural and cultural significance.
Jacob Myers Park, the largest park in Riverbank, offers public access to the Stanislaus River and hosts community events.
Riverbank’s official slogan, “City of Action,” reflects its early 20th‑century growth and ongoing community spirit.
